text.p: Following are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Pakistan has announced the schedule for February 3 elections according to which returning officers will start receiving nomination papers from Tuesday.
- The government has approved changes in the Banks Act to allow the government to seek lists of loan defaulters from private banks and financial institutions.
- Most textile units are working below 40 percent of capacity and not one processes cloth to international standards.

- The International Monetary Fund disagreed with some budgetary measures announced by the caretaker government since completing agreement on November 14 with visiting IMF officials for the revival of the suspended standby arrangement.
- World Bank-led donors have told Pakistan it will get $800 million for the early execution of the Social Action Programme.
- Two foreign pre-shipment inspection companies disclosed a gap of 28 billion rupees ($696 million) in import duty assessed and actually collected by customs over 21 months.
- The IMF is likely to approve the release of $160 million to Pakistan under the stalled standby arrangement. The amount will be released in two tranches of $80 million each.
- The Privatisation Commission has engaged the International Finance Corporation for the privatisation of Pakistan International Airlines.
- Members of the Lahore Chamber of Commerce and Industry exchanged kicks, blows and hot words at their annual general meeting.
- Pakistani traders protested at the road tax of 25,000 rupees ($621) per truck-load levied in Pakistan on imports from China and Central Asian Republics.
- The Malaysian Cocoa Board urged Pakistan to reduce import duties on cocoa to make it competitive for confectionery makers.
- The Pakistan National Shipping Corporation is going to scrap a third ship, Ocean Envoy, after dispensing with Hunza and Kaptai this earlier this year.
- Union Texas Pakistan Inc will start deep drilling of an exploratory oil and gas well in Sindh province early next year.
